_comment: The application commit this workflow is approved to deploy.
A 40-hex app_sha input establishes SYNTAX, not approval. Every commit on
every branch is 40 hex characters. This file is the approval, it lives on
the default branch, and changing it is a reviewed change.
The candidate checkout never supplies its own approval: this file is read
from the operational checkout (the commit the workflow itself ran from),
never from the application commit under deployment.
Future acceptances are a one-line edit here, reviewed like any other.
packageLabel: Expo package: kiosk link control, truthful email verification state, follow-along movement screen at /move, and station enrolment (a second screen at an event, approved by a Champion, showing exactly what the public display shows)
_expectedPriorFunctionsNote: The WSF inventory staging is expected to carry BEFORE this deployment: 24 functions — the same 24 the previous candidate (77bda41) deployed against and left unchanged, since that candidate added no callable. This candidate ADDS SEVEN: wsfStationRequestPairing, wsfStationPairingStatus, wsfApproveStation, wsfStationClaimPairing, wsfStationState, wsfListStations and wsfRevokeStation, so the post-deploy inventory verify-deployment.mjs requires is 31. Four of the seven are unauthenticated by design — a screen at an event is not signed in as anybody — and each is rate limited per IP; the other three are Champion-only. Their Cloud Run transport is REPORTED in the run notes, not asserted, exactly as Package E's and the previous candidate's new services were, because whether a new service needs the approved transport change is established by exercising the callable and the escalation is a separate approval. wsfGoalPulse keeps its nine-field contract: its body moved verbatim into a shared readGoalPulseTotals so wsfStationState answers with exactly it rather than a second implementation of the display gate. Reviewed per candidate; the next package will have a different prior count.
